SMTO-EXE-0247 — This Docker job is too big for SMTO's limits

GUID: e9acf676-a3b2-5029-b6dd-f6f17f6fec53
Slug: docker-resource-limit-exceeded
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: docker

What happened

  • The Docker job was larger than SMTO allows, for example a build folder with too many files, too much output, or too many Docker jobs running at the same time on that Gateway.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you were building an image, add a .dockerignore file to the build folder that leaves out large folders such as .git, node_modules or data files. Builds can include at most 64 MB and 10,000 files from the folder.
  2. If you asked for logs or lists, ask SMTO for less, for example the last 200 log lines or only running containers. Very large answers are refused rather than cut off in a way that could hide important details.
  3. If you were cleaning up, ask SMTO to clean up one kind of item at a time, such as only stopped containers. A single cleanup can cover at most 500 items.
  4. If other Docker tasks are running on the same Gateway, wait for them to finish before trying again. A Gateway runs at most four Docker actions at the same time.

What success looks like

  • The smaller request runs and SMTO shows its result.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway computer, mentioning what you were building or listing. Don't split a build folder in ways that leave out files the image actually needs.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Docker operation exceeded a fixed limit: build context over 64 MiB or 10,000 entries, more than 500 prune or build-cache candidates, oversized Engine, Compose or result data, oversized private values, or more than four Docker operations active on the Gateway at once.

What this means

  • Docker work exceeded context-file/byte count, cache/prune candidate count, wire/result/private-value bounds, subprocess output limits or active-operation capacity. Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Docker work exceeded context-file/byte count, cache/prune candidate count, wire/result/private-value bounds, subprocess output limits or active-operation capacity.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the exact context, output, candidate or concurrency bound; never clip an identity or deletion plan to make it appear valid.

How to fix it

  • Reduce the specific bounded scope: add a .dockerignore to shrink the build context, narrow list/log requests (limit, tail, since), prune one category at a time, keep private values under 64 KiB, or wait for active Docker operations on the Gateway to finish (max four concurrent). If a change had started, inspect its state before resubmitting.
  • Reduce the specific bounded scope or wait for owned work to settle; preserve exact plans, identities and required output.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the exact object identity, typed arguments and selected Gateway capability; correct the reported prerequisite before a new request.

How to verify the fix

  • A complete valid smaller scope or settled capacity fits the supported bound.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain Docker mutation.

Technical notes

  • Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
